dedupe_keys.name: methane emissions from coal mine closure in china under different scenarios gridded annual

description: This dataset maps methane emissions from coal mines in China under different mine closure scenarios, showing the potential for emission reductions and regional differences as producing mines are phased out. The figshare page says it starts from a list of 2,816 producing mines in 2020 from China's National Energy Administration, with production capacity, years of production, mine area and location, which the authors georeferenced with Baidu Maps, matched one by one across sources by name and coordinates, and turned into a dynamic time series per mine. It was published on 26 October 2024 by Lin Gang as a ZIP of GeoTIFF rasters of about 2.8 MB, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, with annual time steps and a spatial resolution of 0.008 degrees; a copy is on Science Data Bank. Coverage is national for China's coal mines. Caveats: the scenario definitions, the year span and the emission factors are not stated on the page read, and closed-mine emissions are modelled, not measured. For simulation it gives gridded methane paths for coal phase-out scenarios, and the underlying mine list helps place coal supply sites when testing energy supply disruption. Related catalogue records include the China coal methane emissions 2011-2019 inventory, the India and Australia coal mine methane inventory and the US underground coal mine methane data.
